title: Ecosystems and Energy Flow
subject: Biology
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET / NEET • Quick Revision

nodes.title: Ecosystem Concept, Stratification & Standing Crop
points: Ecosystem (A.G. Tansley, 1935): Self-regulating, self-sustaining structural and functional unit of the biosphere where living organisms interact among themselves and with the physical environment.

Stratification: Vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels in an ecosystem (e.g. in a forest: Trees form top canopy stratum, Shrubs form middle layer, Herbs/grasses occupy ground layer).
Standing Crop: Total mass of living organisms (biomass) in a unit area at a given time; measured as fresh weight or dry weight (dry weight is more accurate).
Standing State: Total amount of inorganic nutrients (C, N, P, Ca) present in soil at any given time.

formulas.label: Ecosystem stratification hierarchy (Forest)
formulas.expr: Canopy trees (Top stratum) → Understory shrubs (Middle) → Herbs & grasses (Ground stratum)

formulas.label: Standing Crop vs Standing State
formulas.expr: Standing Crop = Living biomass (dry weight) | Standing State = Inorganic nutrients present in soil

nodes.title: Productivity (GPP & NPP) & Decomposition Process
points: Primary Productivity: Rate of biomass production per unit area by producers via photosynthesis (g/m²/yr or kcal/m²/yr). Gross Primary Productivity (GPP): Total rate of organic matter synthesis. Net Primary Productivity (NPP): GPP minus respiratory losses (R): NPP = GPP − R.

Global Biosphere NPP: ~170 billion tons dry weight annually. Oceans cover 70% surface but contribute only 55 billion tons due to light and nutrient limitation; Land contributes ~115 billion tons on 30% area.

Decomposition of Detritus (5 Steps): 1) Fragmentation: Detritivores (earthworm) break detritus into smaller particles; 2) Leaching: Water-soluble inorganic nutrients sink into soil horizons as unavailable salts; 3) Catabolism: Fungal and bacterial enzymes degrade detritus into simpler inorganic substances; 4) Humification: Dark amorphous colloid Humus forms (nutrient reservoir, resistant to microbes); 5) Mineralization: Slow microbial degradation of humus releasing inorganic minerals.

formulas.label: Primary productivity fundamental relation
formulas.expr: NPP = GPP − R (where NPP = Net Primary Productivity, GPP = Gross Primary Productivity, R = Respiration loss)

formulas.label: Decomposition 5-step sequential pathway
formulas.expr: Detritus → Fragmentation (Earthworm) → Leaching → Catabolism (Enzymes) → Humification → Mineralization

formulas.label: Global annual NPP division
formulas.expr: Total Biosphere = ~170 billion tons | Terrestrial (30% area) = ~115 billion tons | Oceans (70% area) = ~55 billion tons

nodes.title: Energy Flow & Lindeman's 10% Law
points: Energy flow is strictly Unidirectional (Sun → Producers → Herbivores → Carnivores). Governed by Laws of Thermodynamics.

Photosynthetically Active Radiation (PAR): Wavelength 400-700 nm; constitutes < 50% of incident solar radiation. Plants capture only 2-10% of PAR (1-5% of total incident solar energy) to sustain entire living biosphere.

Lindeman's 10% Law (1942): Only ~10% of energy entering a trophic level is transferred and incorporated into biomass at the next trophic level; remaining 90% is dissipated as metabolic heat and respiration.
Trophic level designations: T1 (Producers), T2 (Herbivores / Primary consumers), T3 (Secondary consumers), T4 (Tertiary consumers / Top carnivores).

formulas.label: Solar radiation partitioning
formulas.expr: Total Solar Radiation → PAR (< 50%) → Captured by Plants (2 - 10% of PAR)

formulas.label: Lindeman's 10% Energy Transfer Law
formulas.expr: Energy at next trophic level = 0.10 × Energy at current trophic level (90% lost as heat)

formulas.label: Trophic energy cascade numerical example
formulas.expr: Producers (10,000 J) → Herbivores (1,000 J) → Carnivores (100 J) → Top Carnivores (10 J)

nodes.title: Food Chains: Grazing (GFC) vs Detritus (DFC) & Food Web
points: 1. Grazing Food Chain (GFC): Starts with living photosynthetic green plants: Grass (T1) → Deer (T2) → Tiger (T3). Major channel of energy flow in AQUATIC ecosystems.
2. Detritus Food Chain (DFC): Starts with dead organic matter (detritus): Fallen leaves → Earthworm / Maggots → Birds / Frog → Hawk. Major channel of energy flow in TERRESTRIAL ecosystems.
DFC is interconnected with GFC at several levels (e.g. omnivores like cockroaches, crows, humans).
Food Web: Complex network of interconnected food chains; increases ecosystem stability by providing alternative food pathways when one species declines.

formulas.label: Grazing Food Chain (GFC) sequence
formulas.expr: Producers (Grass) → Primary Consumers (Deer) → Secondary Consumers (Tiger)

formulas.label: Detritus Food Chain (DFC) sequence
formulas.expr: Dead Organic Matter (Detritus) → Decomposers / Detritivores → Predators

formulas.label: Aquatic vs Terrestrial dominant food chain
formulas.expr: Aquatic ecosystem = GFC dominant | Terrestrial ecosystem = DFC dominant

nodes.title: Ecological Pyramids: Number, Biomass & Energy
points: Ecological Pyramids (Charles Elton, 1927):
1. Pyramid of Numbers: Upright in grassland (grasses >> herbivores >> carnivores); Inverted in single tree supporting thousands of birds and millions of parasites.

2. Pyramid of Biomass: Upright in terrestrial ecosystems (tree/grass biomass >> herbivores >> carnivores); INVERTED in Aquatic / Ocean ecosystems (standing biomass of phytoplankton is far smaller than zooplankton and predatory fishes!).
3. Pyramid of Energy: ALWAYS UPRIGHT in all ecosystems without exception! Can never be inverted because energy is lost as heat at every step.
Limitations of pyramids: Ignores food webs; excludes saprophytes and decomposers; assumes simple linear food chains; does not accommodate omnivores.

formulas.label: Ecological pyramid shapes summary
formulas.expr: Pyramid of Energy = ALWAYS UPRIGHT | Pyramid of Biomass in sea = INVERTED | Pyramid of Numbers on single tree = INVERTED

formulas.label: Inverted biomass pyramid in sea
formulas.expr: Phytoplankton (lowest biomass, high turnover) < Zooplankton < Fishes (highest biomass)

nodes.title: Ecological Succession: Primary vs Secondary
points: Ecological Succession: Orderly, predictable, progressive change in species composition of a given area over time culminating in a stable Climax Community.

Pioneer Community: First species to colonize a barren area. Seral Stages (Sere): Transitional intermediate communities. Climax Community: Stable, self-perpetuating terminal community in equilibrium with climate.
Primary Succession: Occurs on sterile, bare sites where no life previously existed (bare rock, newly cooled lava, sand dune, new water reservoir). Very slow (takes centuries to build soil).
Secondary Succession: Occurs in areas where a biological community was destroyed by fire, flood, clear-cutting. Much faster because soil and propagules are already present.

formulas.label: Succession developmental sequence
formulas.expr: Pioneer Community → Seral Stages (Seres) → Climax Community (stable, mesic forest)

formulas.label: Primary vs Secondary succession contrast
formulas.expr: Primary: Sterile site, no soil, very slow (centuries) | Secondary: Pre-existing soil present, much faster

nodes.title: Hydrarch & Xerarch Succession Pathways
points: 1. Hydrarch Succession (in aquatic habitat): Phytoplankton pioneer (diatoms) → Submerged rooted stage (Hydrilla, Vallisneria) → Rooted floating stage (Nymphaea, Nelumbo) → Free-floating stage (Pistia, Eichhornia) → Reed-Swamp stage (Typha, Phragmites) → Marsh-Meadow stage (Cyperus, Carex) → Scrub stage (Salix) → Climax Mesic Forest.

2. Xerarch Succession (on bare rock): Crustose lichens pioneer (Rhizocarpon, secrete acids to weather rock) → Foliose lichens (Parmelia) → Moss stage (Polytrichum, Funaria) → Annual herbs → Perennial grasses → Shrubs → Climax Mesic Forest.
Convergence Principle: Both Hydrarch (wet) and Xerarch (dry) successions converge towards the same medium moisture condition — a MESIC Climax Community!

formulas.label: Hydrarch succession 7-stage pathway
formulas.expr: Phytoplankton → Submerged → Floating → Reed-Swamp → Marsh-Meadow → Scrub → Climax Forest

formulas.label: Xerarch succession 6-stage pathway
formulas.expr: Crustose lichens → Foliose lichens → Mosses → Herbs → Shrubs → Climax Forest

formulas.label: Convergence principle of succession
formulas.expr: Hydric (excess water) & Xeric (scant water) both lead to MESIC (moderate water) Climax

nodes.title: Biogeochemical Cycles: Carbon & Phosphorus Cycles
points: Nutrient Cycling: Gaseous (Atmosphere/ocean reservoir e.g. Carbon, Nitrogen) vs Sedimentary (Lithosphere / rock reservoir e.g. Phosphorus, Sulfur).

1. Carbon Cycle: Carbon constitutes 49% dry weight of organisms. 71% of global carbon is dissolved in Oceans; ~1% in atmosphere. ~4 × 10¹³ kg carbon fixed annually by photosynthesis; returned by respiration, decomposition, fossil fuel combustion.

2. Phosphorus Cycle (Sedimentary): Component of nucleic acids, ATP, biological membranes, bones, teeth. Reservoir: Rocks. Weathering releases phosphate into soil → plant uptake → food chains → decomposers. Lacks gaseous atmospheric phase; atmospheric inputs negligible.

formulas.label: Global carbon distribution
formulas.expr: Oceans (71% dissolved carbon) | Atmosphere (1% CO₂) | Biomass (49% dry weight is Carbon)

formulas.label: Photosynthetic carbon fixation annual rate
formulas.expr: 4 × 10¹³ kg of carbon fixed annually in biosphere via photosynthesis

formulas.label: Carbon vs Phosphorus cycle contrast
formulas.expr: Carbon: Gaseous, atmospheric reservoir, respiratory exchange | Phosphorus: Sedimentary (rock reservoir), no gaseous phase

nodes.title: High-Weightage Board Questions & Ecosystem Services
points: Board Q1: State Lindeman's 10% law of energy transfer and explain why a pyramid of energy is always upright.
Board Q2: Describe the 5 steps involved in the process of decomposition of detritus.
Board Q3: Differentiate between Primary and Secondary succession. Describe the stages of Xerarch succession.
Board Q4: Explain why the pyramid of biomass in an aquatic (ocean) ecosystem is inverted.

Ecosystem Services (Robert Costanza, 1997): Global life-support services valued at ~\$33 trillion / year (nearly double global GNP of \$18 trillion): Soil formation accounts for ~50%, Recreation/nutrient cycling ~10% each, Climate regulation ~6%.

formulas.label: Robert Costanza ecosystem services valuation
formulas.expr: Global nature services = \$33 trillion / year (Soil formation ~50% | Recreation/Nutrients ~10% each | Climate ~6%)

formulas.label: Decomposition rate controlling factors
formulas.expr: Faster if detritus is rich in Nitrogen & sugars | Slower if rich in Lignin & Chitin | Favored by warm, moist climate

nodes.title: MHT-CET & NEET High-Speed Shortcuts & Traps
points: TRAP 1: Inverted pyramid of biomass: Ocean / lake ecosystem has an INVERTED biomass pyramid because phytoplankton have very small standing biomass at any one time compared to longer-lived fishes, despite high productivity!
TRAP 2: Pyramid of energy CAN NEVER BE INVERTED under any circumstance!

TRAP 3: Oceans vs Land productivity: Oceans cover ~70% of earth's surface but produce only 55 billion tons of dry biomass (out of 170 billion tons total biosphere NPP). Terrestrial land produces ~115 billion tons (68% of global NPP) on only 30% area!
TRAP 4: Pioneers in Xerarch vs Hydrarch: Xerarch pioneer = Crustose lichens; Hydrarch pioneer = Phytoplankton.
TRAP 5: Reservoir of phosphorus is ROCKS (sedimentary), whereas reservoir of carbon is OCEANS (71% dissolved) and atmosphere.

formulas.label: Biosphere productivity disparity
formulas.expr: Oceans (70% area) = 55 billion tons NPP | Land (30% area) = 115 billion tons NPP

formulas.label: Ecological succession pioneer pairs
formulas.expr: Xerarch (bare rock) = Crustose lichens | Hydrarch (water body) = Phytoplankton

formulas.label: Energy pyramid inviolability
formulas.expr: Pyramid of energy is ALWAYS UPRIGHT due to 2nd Law of Thermodynamics
